fields.label: Title
fields.default: How a sigh changed our roadmap

fields.name: intro
fields.label: Intro
fields.default:
In 2019 we were three researchers at a Toronto agency, writing reports that ran to forty pages. Clients thanked us, filed them and moved on.

Then a client watched a fifteen-second clip of a customer sighing at their checkout page. They rebuilt the page that month. We started Fieldnote the month after.

fields.name: more
fields.label: Rest of the story
fields.default:
The first version was a spreadsheet of timestamps and a shared folder of video. It was clumsy, but teams used it every week, which was more than anyone had done with our reports.

We spent the next year turning that habit into a product: recordings that transcribe themselves, tags that work across studies, and clips anyone can play without an account.

Today more than twelve hundred teams use Fieldnote. The idea has not changed. Keep the customer’s own words, keep them short, and put them where decisions are made.
